hello-world.title: Hello, world
hello-world.description: The classic first program. Every Luau script can call print.

comments.title: Comments
comments.description: Comments are notes for you (and future-you) — Luau ignores them.

statements.title: Statements
statements.description: Semicolons are optional. One statement per line is the usual style.

local-variables.title: Local variables
local-variables.description: Declare values with local. Locals stay inside the block they live in.

reassigning.title: Reassigning variables
reassigning.description: Variables hold one value at a time — you can change what they hold.

main-types.title: The main types
main-types.description: Numbers, strings, booleans, and nil are the core building blocks.

type-checking.title: Check a value's type
type-checking.description: type() returns the name of a value's type as a string.

multiple-assignment.title: Multiple assignment
multiple-assignment.description: Assign several variables at once, and use it to swap values.

string-basics.title: String basics
string-basics.description: Text in Luau is a string. Double or single quotes both work.

interpolation.title: String interpolation
interpolation.description: Backticks let you embed values directly inside a string.

string-methods.title: Common string helpers
string-methods.description: The string library covers the day-to-day text operations.

arithmetic.title: Arithmetic
arithmetic.description: The usual math, plus floor division and remainder.

comparison.title: Comparison
comparison.description: Compare values for equality and ordering. ~= means "not equal".

boolean-logic.title: Boolean logic
boolean-logic.description: and, or, and not combine true/false conditions.

compound-assignment.title: Compound assignment
compound-assignment.description: Shorthand for updating a variable with an operation.

if-else.title: if / elseif / else
if-else.description: Run different code depending on a condition.

while-loop.title: while loop
while-loop.description: Repeat while a condition stays true.

numeric-for.title: Numeric for loop
numeric-for.description: Count up (or down) over a range. A third number sets the step.

break.title: break
break.description: Exit a loop early from inside it.

define-call.title: Define & call
define-call.description: Bundle code into a named function, then call it with arguments.

return-values.title: Return values
return-values.description: A function can hand a value back to whoever called it.

multiple-returns.title: Multiple returns
multiple-returns.description: Return several values at once and capture them all.

anonymous-functions.title: Anonymous functions
anonymous-functions.description: Functions are values too — pass them around as callbacks.

varargs.title: Varargs
varargs.description: ... accepts any number of extra arguments.

create-index.title: Create & index
create-index.description: Tables hold multiple values. Lists start at index 1; dictionaries use keys.

dictionary-iteration.title: Iterate a dictionary
dictionary-iteration.description: pairs() visits every key and value.

list-iteration.title: Iterate a list
list-iteration.description: ipairs() walks a list in order, 1 to #list.

table-methods.title: Table helpers
table-methods.description: table.insert and table.remove keep lists tidy.

task-wait.title: task.wait
task-wait.description: Pause the current script for a number of seconds.

task-spawn.title: task.spawn
task-spawn.description: Run a function without blocking the code after it.

warn.title: warn
warn.description: Print a message that stands out in the Output window.

common-mistakes.title: Common mistakes
common-mistakes.description: The two errors beginners hit most: = instead of == and a missing end.

part.title: Part
part.body: A 3D object in the game world — walls, blocks, coins. Parts are the LEGO bricks every Roblox build is made of.

instance.title: Instance
instance.body: Any object in a Roblox place — a part, a script, a sound, a folder. Everything in the Explorer tree is an instance.

instancing.title: Instancing
instancing.body: Creating instances at runtime with Instance.new() so the game builds parts and objects while it runs.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.body: The container in the game that holds everything visible in the world. Scripts parent parts here to make them appear.

script.title: Script
script.body: A file of Luau code that runs in a game. Scripts run on the server and control what happens in the world.

local-script.title: Local script
local-script.body: A script that runs on each player's own device. Local scripts handle input, the camera, and the UI.

module-script.title: Module script
module-script.body: A script that other scripts can load to share code — one copy of a function used in many places.

variable.title: Variable
variable.body: A named box that holds a value — a number, a string, a part, anything. You create one with local.

function.title: Function
function.body: A named block of code that runs when you call it. Functions let you reuse logic instead of repeating it.

table.title: Table
table.body: A container that holds many values at once. Lists start at index 1; dictionaries pair keys with values.

array.title: Array
array.body: A table that holds an ordered list of values, each with a number index starting at 1.

dictionary.title: Dictionary
dictionary.body: A table that stores key-value pairs, so you look values up by a name instead of a number.

loop.title: Loop
loop.body: A block that repeats its code. A for loop counts through values; a while loop runs until a condition turns false.

for-loop.title: For loop
for-loop.body: A loop that runs a known number of times, counting up or down through a range of numbers.

while-loop.title: While loop
while-loop.body: A loop that keeps running while a condition is true and stops the moment it turns false.

if-statement.title: If statement
if-statement.body: A block that runs code only when a condition is true, with optional elseif and else branches.

condition.title: Condition
condition.body: A true/false question the code checks — a comparison like score > 100, or a boolean value.

operator.title: Operator
operator.body: A symbol that works on values: math (+), comparisons (==), and logic (and, or, not).

event.title: Event
event.body: Something that happens in the game — a player joining, a part touched. You listen with :Connect().

event-handler.title: Event handler
event-handler.body: The function that runs when an event fires. You connect it to the event to respond to it.

tween.title: Tween
tween.body: A smooth, timed animation of a property — moving a part from A to B over seconds instead of jumping.

cframe.title: CFrame
cframe.body: A value that holds a position and a rotation together. Used to place and point parts precisely.

property.title: Property
property.body: A setting on an instance — size, color, position, name. You read and change them with a dot.

player.title: Player
player.body: A person in your game. The Players service tracks them, and their character is their avatar in the world.

leaderstats.title: Leaderstats
leaderstats.body: A folder that shows numbers in the on-screen leaderboard — like coins, score, or level.

datastore.title: DataStore
datastore.body: A Roblox cloud save that stores values between sessions, so progress survives a player leaving.

remote-event.title: Remote event
remote-event.body: A safe way for the server and a player's device to send signals to each other.

debounce.title: Debounce
debounce.body: A guard that stops a function from running twice in a row — like one reward per part touch.

vector.title: Vector
vector.body: A value with three numbers — x, y, z — used for positions, sizes, and directions.

raycast.title: Raycast
raycast.body: Firing an invisible ray from a point in a direction to ask the world what's in the way — used for line of sight, ground checks, and lasers.

particle-emitter.title: Particle Emitter
particle-emitter.body: An object that spawns small visual particles from a part — sparkles, smoke, fire, and other effects that make a game feel alive.

proximity-prompt.title: Proximity Prompt
proximity-prompt.body: A floating 'E to interact' prompt that appears when a player walks near a part — the modern way to let players interact with doors, NPCs, and objects.

pcall.title: pcall
pcall.body: Protected call — runs a function and catches errors instead of crashing the script, essential for safe DataStore calls.

string-pattern.title: String Pattern
string-pattern.body: A mini language for matching text inside strings — find words, extract numbers, replace parts of a message using codes like %d (digits) and %a (letters).

animation-track.title: Animation Track
animation-track.body: An object that plays a Roblox animation on a character — load it from the Animator, then call :Play() to make the character move.

pathfinding.title: Pathfinding
pathfinding.body: Using PathfindingService to calculate a walkable route around obstacles so an NPC can move from point A to point B.

lighting.title: Lighting
lighting.body: The service that controls global light, sky, fog, and post-processing effects — the mood and atmosphere of your entire game.

metatable.title: Metatable
metatable.body: A hidden table attached to another table that intercepts operations like indexing, letting you build OOP patterns — constructors, inheritance, and custom behavior.

team.title: Team
team.body: A grouping from the Teams service that puts players on sides — red vs blue, survivors vs infected — controlling spawn location and scoreboards.

q1.question: What does the print function do in Luau?

options.2: Outputs text to the Output window

q1.explanation: print() writes text to Studio's Output window — your first debugging tool.

q2.question: How do you write a single-line comment in Luau?
q2.explanation: Luau uses -- for comments. // is C-style and is not valid Luau.

q3.question: Which keyword creates a new local variable?

q4.question: What does the # operator return when applied to a string?
q4.explanation: #"hello" returns 5 — the length of the string in bytes.

q5.question: What is the value of "10" + 5 in Luau?
q5.explanation: Luau automatically coerces numeric strings in arithmetic, so "10" + 5 is 15.

q6.question: What does the % operator do?

options.1: Returns the remainder of a division

q6.explanation: The modulo operator gives the remainder, e.g. 7 % 3 is 1.

q7.question: Which operator joins two strings together?

q9.question: After local x = 10 and then x = x + 5, what is x?

q10.question: What does type(true) return?
q10.explanation: type() returns a string describing the value's type.

q11.question: Which values are 'truthy' in Luau?
q11.explanation: Only false and nil are falsy — even 0 and empty strings are truthy.

q12.question: What does nil represent in Luau?

q13.question: What is the difference between = and ==?

q14.question: What is the result of true and false?

q15.question: What is the result of not false?

q16.question: Which values make if x then run its block?

q17.question: When does if health <= 0 then run?

options.0: When health is zero or negative

q18.question: What is the purpose of elseif?

options.0: Check another condition when the previous was false

q19.question: How does every if statement end in Luau?

q20.question: What does local x = false and error("boom") evaluate to?
q20.explanation: and short-circuits: when the left side is falsy, the right side is never evaluated.

q21.question: How many times does the body of for i = 1, 5 do run?

q22.question: What values does for i = 1, 5, 2 do produce?
q22.explanation: A step of 2 skips every other value, ending at 5.

q23.question: A while true do loop with no exit condition will…

q24.question: In repeat ... until condition, when is the condition checked?

options.1: After the body runs (at least once)

q25.question: What does break do inside a loop?

q26.question: What skips the rest of the current iteration in a Luau loop?
q26.explanation: Luau supports continue to jump to the next iteration.

q27.question: How do you define a function named heal?

q28.question: What keyword sends a value back out of a function?

q29.question: A function that never hits return returns…

q30.question: In local function add(a, b) what are a and b?

q31.question: What does ... mean in a function like local function log(...)?

options.0: It accepts any number of extra arguments

q31.explanation: The variadic ... lets a function accept extra arguments.

q32.question: Calling part:SetPosition() instead of part.SetPosition(part) — what does the : do?

options.1: Passes part as the first argument (self)

q32.explanation: The colon passes the instance itself as the first argument, known as self.

q33.question: In Luau, what is the index of the first element of an array?

q34.question: What is #{10, 20, 30}?
q34.explanation: # returns the length of an array-like table.

q35.question: If t = {name = "Ada"}, how else can you write t.name?

options.1: Appends x to the end of t

q40.question: What is the result of 5 // 2 in Luau?
q40.explanation: // is floor division — it rounds down, so 5 // 2 is 2.

q44.question: Where are the parts in a game's world stored?

q45.question: Which service tracks the players in your game?

q47.question: How do you get a player's character model?

q49.question: Which event fires when one part touches another?

q50.question: What does CFrame.new(0, 10, 0) describe?
q50.explanation: A CFrame stores both a position and a rotation in 3D space.

d1.question: local t = {}; t[1] = "a"; t[2] = "b". What does #t return?
d1.explanation: # returns the length of the array part; both slots are filled, so it's 2 — not "ab".

d2.question: After local a, b = 1, what is the value of b?
d2.explanation: Assigning fewer values than names leaves the rest as nil — b was never given a value.

d3.question: What does math.floor(-2.7) return?
d3.explanation: floor rounds toward negative infinity, so -2.7 becomes -3.

d4.question: You need a part named "Door" to exist before your script continues. Which line waits safely?
d4.explanation: WaitForChild yields until the named child exists. The busy while loop never yields, so it locks up the thread.

d5.question: What is the value of 1 .. 2?
d5.explanation: .. always concatenates — the numbers are coerced to strings, giving "12", not 3.

d6.question: What does type(CFrame.new()) return?
d6.explanation: CFrame is its own type in Luau, so type() returns the string "CFrame".

d7.question: local x = 10; if x == 10 then x = 20 elseif true then x = 30 end — what is x?
d7.explanation: Once the first branch runs, the rest of the elseif chain is skipped — 30 is never assigned.

d8.question: What does #{nil} return?
d8.explanation: nil occupies no slot, so the sequence is empty and its length is 0.

d9.question: Which sequence does for i = 5, 1, -1 do visit?
d9.explanation: A negative step counts down and stops when i drops below 1.

d10.question: local t = {10, 20, 30}. After table.remove(t, 1), what is #t?
d10.explanation: table.remove shifts the remaining elements down, so the array becomes {20, 30} with length 2.

d11.question: What's the real difference between wait() and task.wait()?

options.1: task.wait() uses the task scheduler and can wait less than 0.03s

d11.explanation: task.wait() runs on the newer task scheduler and has no 0.03s minimum, while legacy wait() clamps to it.

d12.question: Which of these runs on the player's device (client)?
d12.explanation: LocalScripts run on the client. ModuleScripts only run when required by another script.

d13.question: How many arguments does string.gsub need at minimum?
d13.explanation: string.gsub(source, pattern, replacement) needs three: the string, a pattern, and what to substitute.

d14.question: Which event fires once per frame on the client?
d14.explanation: Heartbeat fires every rendered frame. The others only fire on their specific events.

d15.question: What does string.rep("ab", 3) return?
d15.explanation: rep repeats the string the given number of times — "ab" three times is "ababab".

d16.question: Which loop always runs its body at least once?
d16.explanation: repeat...until checks its condition after the body, so the body always runs at least once.

d17.question: What does table.concat({1, 2, 3}, ", ") return?
d17.explanation: concat joins each element with the separator, coercing the numbers to strings.

d18.question: Which of these is NOT a valid way to create a Vector3?
d18.explanation: Vector3 takes exactly three numbers — the fourth form raises an error. (Two-arg and zero forms are valid shortcuts.)

d19.question: How do you stop a connected event from firing again?
d19.explanation: RBXScriptConnection has a Disconnect method. Setting the variable to nil doesn't stop the event.

d20.question: What does os.clock() measure?

options.1: CPU time used by the running program

d20.explanation: os.clock() returns CPU time consumed by the program — useful for timing how long code actually took.

d21.question: What happens when you run if 0 then print("yes") end?
d21.explanation: Only false and nil are falsy. 0, empty strings, and empty tables are all truthy in Luau.

d22.question: local x = 5; local x = 10; print(x) — what prints?

options.2: An error — x is already declared

d22.explanation: The second local shadows the first in the same scope, so x is 10 when printed.

d23.question: What does print(math.huge > 1000) print?
d23.explanation: math.huge is infinity, and infinity is greater than any finite number.

d24.question: local ok, err = pcall(function() error("boom") end). What is ok?
d24.explanation: pcall returns false as its first value when the function errors, plus the error message.

d25.question: game:GetService("TweenService"):Create(part, TweenInfo.new(1), {...}) — what is missing before it animates?
d25.explanation: Tweens are created paused; you must call :Play() to start the animation.

debug-nil-part.question: What's the bug?

options.0: The script is missing a local variable
options.1: SpawnPart doesn't exist, so part is nil
options.3: print needs a string, not a number

debug-nil-part.explanation: workspace.SpawnPart is nil when no part named SpawnPart exists — you can't read .Position off nil. Use WaitForChild("SpawnPart") or check with FindFirstChild first.

debug-arithmetic-nil.question: What's the bug?

options.0: Can't add to nil — coins has no starting value
options.1: The variable name has a typo
options.3: local must come after the assignment

debug-arithmetic-nil.explanation: coins was declared without a value, so it's nil, and nil + 10 is an error. Give it a real start: local coins = 0.

debug-call-nil.question: What's the bug?

options.1: Functions must be called with a colon
options.2: makeCoins isn't defined yet — it's nil
options.3: The script is missing a require

debug-call-nil.explanation: You can't call nil. Define the function before calling it — and double-check the spelling. Scripts run top to bottom.

debug-undefined-global.question: What's the bug?

options.1: coin doesn't exist — you meant coins

debug-undefined-global.explanation: coin (no s) was never declared. Studio warns "Undefined global" — variable names must match exactly.

debug-missing-end.question: What's the bug?

options.0: Missing end to close the if block
options.2: print can't be called inside an if

debug-missing-end.explanation: Every if needs a matching end. Studio reports "Expected end" and points at the line where the block opened.

debug-string-concat.question: What's the bug?
debug-string-concat.explanation: + is for arithmetic. To join strings in Luau use ..: print("Hello " .. name).

debug-zero-index.question: What's the bug?

options.0: items[0] is nil — Luau arrays start at 1

debug-zero-index.explanation: Luau arrays are 1-indexed. items[1] is "sword" and items[0] is nil.

debug-localplayer.question: What's the bug?

options.0: LocalPlayer only exists on the client — it's nil on the server
options.3: You need to require the Players service

debug-localplayer.explanation: The server has no single "LocalPlayer" — it sees all players. On the server, use game.Players.PlayerAdded instead.

debug-character-nil.question: What's the bug?

options.0: Character doesn't exist yet — it spawns after joining
options.2: PlayerAdded only fires on the client
options.3: The character needs to be cloned manually

debug-character-nil.explanation: A player's Character is nil until it loads. Wait for CharacterAdded, then WaitForChild("Humanoid").

debug-infinite-loop.question: What's the bug?

options.0: The loop never ends, so print never runs
options.2: while loops need an end keyword

debug-infinite-loop.explanation: while true do with no exit condition and no task.wait() runs forever — the script never reaches print and Studio may freeze.

debug-touch-event.question: What's the bug?

options.0: Touch isn't a property — the event is called Touched and needs :Connect
options.1: Doors can't be touched in code

debug-touch-event.explanation: Events aren't assigned — they're connected with :Connect, and the touch event is called Touched: door.Touched:Connect(function() ... end).

debug-property-typo.question: What's the bug?

options.0: Positon isn't a property — it's Position

debug-property-typo.explanation: Studio reports "Positon is not a valid member". Tiny typos in property names are a classic first bug — and why autocomplete helps.
